crop.notes: Whole article 'The Squared Circle', reprinted from the Cincinnati Times, from the headline to the closing rule, across ten pieces.

ocr.notes: Gist is there but many errors, worst in the fight records (e.g. 'Kectes lles' for George Iles, '562 minutes' for 52, 'pier 32, 1862' for May 12, 'Beat Ben. ‘ee' for Ben Hogan, 'oes 18' for September 18), and the Forest Home section.

title.suggested: Allen and Goss in Training, with Their Fight Records

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reprinted a Cincinnati Times account of Tom Allen and Joe Goss in training for their September 7 fight for $2,500 a side, with the match articles and each man's own fight record.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Monday Morning, July 17, 1876', page 5. Reprinted from the Cincinnati Times.

facts.fact: Allen and Joe Goss signed articles at Eph. Holland's Empire Saloon, Fifth Street near Vine, Cincinnati, to fight under the new London prize ring rules for $2,500 a side on September 7, 1876, within 100 miles of Cincinnati
places: Empire Saloon, Fifth Street near Vine, Cincinnati, Ohio

facts.fact: After the articles were signed, Allen and Goss were bound over before 'Squire Anthony in $500 each to keep the peace in Ohio for one year, to prevent interference while training
Immediately after signing, Allen left Cincinnati to give exhibitions in several prominent Eastern cities
Allen trained for the Goss fight at Cedar Park, John Young's retreat about half a mile south of Carthage, near Cincinnati, under the care of Jack Madden
Goss said he had been matched to fight Harry Allen, Tom Allen's brother, but the fight was stopped by magisterial interference
Allen's own record: Beat White, £5 a side, 12 rounds in 40 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat Morris Connor, £10 a side, 22 rounds in 50 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat Jack Gold, £15 a side, 51 rounds in 1 hour 22 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat Hall, £25 a side, 15 rounds in 42 minutes
Allen's own record: Beaten by Posh Price, £10 a side, 22 rounds in 55 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat 'Bingy' Rose, £25 a side, 10 rounds in 22 minutes
Allen's own record: Beaten by Bob Smith (colored), £5 a side, 108 rounds in 3 hours 57 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat Jack Parkison, £25 a side, 11 rounds in 20 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat Posh Price, £50 a side, 45 rounds in 2 hours 5 minutes
Allen's own record: Beat George Iles, £50 a side, 15 rounds in 52 minutes
Allen's own record: Fought a draw with Joe Goss in Wales, £100 a side, 37 rounds in 1 hour 57 minutes
Allen, with Peter Morris, arrived in America on July 22, 1867, and gave sparring exhibitions in several of the larger cities
Allen's own record: first fight in America: beat Bill Davis, $1,000 a side, 40 rounds in 40 minutes
Allen's own record: beaten by Charley Gallagher, 2 rounds in 3 minutes, $1,000 a side
Allen's own record: fought Mike McCoole, $1,000 a side, 7 rounds in 14 minutes; Allen had the best of it but the ring was broken into and a draw declared
Allen's own record: beat Charley Gallagher, $1,000 a side, 17 rounds in 22 minutes
Allen's own record: beaten by Jem Mace, $1,500 a side, 10 rounds in 44 minutes
Allen's own record: beat Jim Gallagher, $500 a side, 15 rounds in 22 minutes
Allen's own record: received $1,000 forfeit from Mike McCoole
Allen's own record: beat Mike McCoole, $2,500 a side, 8 rounds in 19 minutes
Allen's own record: beat Ben Hogan, 3 rounds in 6 minutes
Allen's own record: matched to fight George Rooke near Pittsburg, but Rooke failed to come to time

notes: Fight records are Allen's own account as printed. The Goss draw is printed as March 5, 1867, the same date given for the Iles fight, so one date is probably wrong. The Hogan fight (September 18, 1873) is listed after the McCoole fight (September 23, 1873). The article also gives Goss's record (born Northampton 1836), not included as facts. Stakeholder printed once as 'A. B. Edwards', elsewhere 'A. F. Edwards'.
